articles.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
articles.summary: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $ν_τ$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. articles.title: JWST Rocky Worlds DDT Observations of LTT 1445 A b and c in Secondary Eclipse Using MIRI/F1500W
articles.summary: The JWST Rocky Worlds Director's Discretionary Time (RWDDT) program uses secondary eclipse observations to determine the conditions under which rocky exoplanets around M dwarfs retain their atmospheres. articles.title: The origin of Potassium in Galactic chemical evolution - The effect of C-O shell mergers in massive stars
articles.summary: The Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of potassium (K) and of most other odd-Z elements remains poorly understood: models generally underproduce the observed [K/Fe] over a wide metallicity range, depending on the adopted massive star yields. articles.summary: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron stars beyond the Galactic Center can be lensed by the supermassive black hole in Sgr A$^*$. articles.summary: Compact millimeter emission from radio-quiet active galactic nuclei has been proposed as a probe of magnetized accretion-disk coronae. articles.title: Lurkers at the Threshold: GWTC-4.0's near-threshold events
articles.summary: We present the first systematic parameter-estimation analysis of 42 candidate gravitational-wave signals identified in GWTC-4.0 with a probability of astrophysical origin $p_\mathrm{astro} \geq 0.5$, but a false-alarm rate of at least $1\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, which were therefore not selected for parameter estimation in the catalogue. articles.title: Stellar-Field-Driven Induction Heating Unlikely To Cause Significant Heating in Giant Exoplanets
articles.summary: A planet moving through a changing magnetic field will have a current induced on it by that magnetic field. If the magnetic Reynolds number in the upper atmosphere of this planet is small, the dissipation of this current could result in observable changes to the planet's properties. In this paper, we estimated the total power that would be dissipated in the observed giant exoplanet population if they orbited stars with misaligned magnetic dipoles. articles.title: Lense-Thirring induced repeating blast trains in continuous gravitational waves
articles.summary: We characterise gravitational lensing induced by the Lense-Thirring effect in a continuous gravitational-wave source orbiting a spinning supermassive black hole. This scenario is very likely to generate lensing events, as long as the source's orbital inclination is not aligned with the black hole's spin axis and the Lense-Thirring timescale is shorter than the observational window. The signal appears as short-duration ($T_{\rm blast}$) gravitational-wave "blasts" that repeat after every orbit ($T_{\rm orb}$) within a limited time window ($T_{\rm train}$). articles.title: Bayesian Inference of Fermionic Dark Matter Admixed Neutron Stars Informed by Galaxy Cluster Constraints
articles.summary: Self-interacting dark matter is constrained on galactic and cluster scales by its elastic scattering cross section per unit mass, $σ/m_χ\sim 0.1-10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. articles.title: The Same But Different: SiO$_2$ Clouds in Two L-Dwarfs with JWST
articles.summary: The precision of brown dwarf spectra from JWST enables unprecedented insight into the atmospheric and cloud properties of sub-stellar atmospheres. articles.summary: The origins and architectures of hot Jupiter (HJ) systems remain unclear, with potential explanations for the tight orbits being in-situ formation, disk-migration, or high-eccentricity migration. articles.title: Global climate modeling of the Martian water cycle. I) Improved parameterizations of physical processes
articles.summary: We implement four new physical parameterizations relevant to the water cycle in the Mars PCM (previously Mars Laboratoire de M{é}t{é}orologie Dynamique GCM)\,: the latent heat of ground ice sublimation, a temperature-dependent nucleation scheme in cloud microphysics, differentiated albedos for water frost and perennial ice and scavenging of water ice clouds by CO2 particle formation. articles.title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
articles.summary: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. articles.title: Efficient Standard Siren Cosmological Inference with Posterior Reuse
articles.summary: Standard siren cosmology depends on several modelling assumptions, including the underlying source population, galaxy catalogue, and detection selection function. Quantifying the effect of each choice typically requires a full, independent analysis. As gravitational-wave catalogs grow incrementally, much computational effort is spent re-analysing largely overlapping datasets. articles.title: Nucleation of water ice under weak ionization via clustering on negative ions
articles.summary: Water-ice grains are shown to form spontaneously in a cold, weakly-ionized laboratory plasma with trace water admixture when neutrals and ions are cooled below $\sim$200 K. The ice grains form without the presence of particulate impurities, and do not form in the absence of ionization, indicating that nucleation is induced by ions. articles.title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A

articles.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
articles.summary: The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) is an in-ice radio observatory at the South Pole designed to detect ultrahigh energy (UHE) neutrinos through Askaryan emission produced by interactions of neutrinos and their secondary particles. In this paper, we present the detailed methodology of the first array-wide search for a diffuse UHE neutrino flux using data from all five ARA stations. articles.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
articles.summary: Ultrahigh energy neutrinos ($E_ν\gtrsim 100$ PeV) are detectable through Askaryan emission---the nanosecond-scale radio impulse emitted by relativistic particle cascades in a dielectric medium. The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA), an Askaryan detector array located at the South Pole, has been taking data for more than a decade. We present the first array-wide search for diffuse ultrahigh energy neutrinos with ARA. articles.summary: Perturbative QCD, supplemented only by thermodynamic consistency, causality, and mechanical stability, constrains the equation of state of dense matter far below the densities at which the perturbative expansion itself converges. articles.summary: I search the single-epoch detections of the NOIRLab Source Catalog DR2 (DECam, 2012-2019) for outer Solar System objects. Single-night detections are linked with a bound orbit model, vetted against artefacts, static sources and known objects, and confirmed by forced measurements on at least two new archival nights. articles.title: Relativistic tidal response and mode excitation in neutron-star binaries
articles.summary: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. articles.title: Unveiling the Extreme Universe with Recent IACT Discoveries
articles.summary: Very-high-energy (VHE, $E \gtrsim 50$\,GeV) $γ$-ray astronomy has evolved into an indispensable pillar of modern astroparticle physics, offering a direct view of non-thermal particle acceleration, cosmic-ray origins, and fundamental physics. articles.title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
articles.summary: Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. articles.title: Spectral-Timing Evolution of the Black Hole X-ray Binary LMC X-3: An XPoSat View
articles.summary: LMC X-3 is a persistent black hole high-mass X-ray binary and serves as an important laboratory for studying accretion disk evolution across different spectral states. We present a spectral-timing analysis of XPoSat/XSPECT observations of LMC X--3 obtained during 2024 and 2025. Using broadband X-ray light curves, hardness diagnostics, power spectral analysis, and spectral modeling, we investigate the long-term evolution of the source across multiple epochs. articles.title: Empirical constraints on cosmic-ray scattering in NGC 1333 from dust polarisation
articles.summary: Cosmic rays (CRs) regulate molecular-cloud ionization and chemistry. Gyro-resonant scattering by magnetic fluctuations sets their mean free path and, on larger scales, their effective diffusion coefficient. articles.title: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
articles.summary: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. articles.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars
articles.summary: Brown dwarfs are rare as close companions to stars compared to planets and stellar companions, a paucity known as the brown dwarf desert. articles.title: Search for a Dispersion Measure Excess Toward Nearby Galaxy Halos Using Fast Radio Bursts from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog
articles.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe foreground ionized baryons via their dispersion measures (DM). articles.title: The Tierras Observatory: Ultra-Precise Photometry for Characterizing Exoplanets and Their Host Stars
articles.summary: The Tierras Observatory is a fully robotic 1.3-m telescope at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in southern Arizona. Tierras achieves sub-part-per-thousand (ppt) photometric precision on two timescales: intra-night, to detect and characterize transits of planets around nearby mid-to-late M dwarfs, and night-to-night across an observing season, to characterize the long-term variability of their host stars. articles.title: AGN Feedback Turbulence in Cool-core Clusters: Evidence from XRISM
articles.summary: The XRISM X-ray Observatory has revealed evidence for a "double-cascade" scenario in the Perseus cluster, in which active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback and mergers drive turbulence over distinct radial ranges and spatial scales. articles.title: Joint Gaia-Hipparcos astrometry, RV, and Imaging posteriors from the G23H Hipparcos sample
articles.summary: We present uniform posteriors indicating the presence or absence of stellar and planetary companions over a sample of $10^5$ stars in Hipparcos and Gaia. articles.title: Simulation of a Jovian Planet Undergoing Gas Accretion

articles.title: MarsNet: Learning the Martian Atmosphere from Observations Alone
articles.summary: We present MarsNet, a machine-learned model of the Martian atmosphere trained only on observations. articles.summary: Young protoplanetary disks have received increasing attention in recent years, due to observations revealing the presence of substructures in disks younger than one million years, suggesting that planet formation may begin earlier than previously thought. Other recent observations have provided new insights into the evolution of gas and dust in these early stages, enabling comparisons with evolved Class II disks. articles.title: The Swift/UVOT Observation Campaign of Comet C/2013 US10 (Catalina) and Near-nucleus UV Excess

articles.title: The Edge of the Warm Corona in Active Galactic Nuclei
articles.summary: A model of warm, dissipative corona on top of an accretion disk is investigated, to explain the soft X-ray excess (SXE) emission observed in active galactic nuclei (AGN). articles.title: The compositional link between rocky exoplanets and their host stars is consistent with Earth-like devolatilization
articles.summary: Previous work found a higher bulk iron-to-silicon (Fe/Si) ratio in rocky exoplanets relative to their host star, traditionally explained by iron enrichment. articles.summary: Thanks to recent measurements by space and ground-level detectors, the energy spectra of cosmic ray protons and helium nuclei are now known with good precision over a broad energy range extending for more than six orders of magnitude, from a few GeV to approximately 10PeV. articles.summary: Asteroids near the boundary between the Atira and 'Ayló'chaxnim classes can trace dynamical links between the two populations, but their small solar elongations make recovery and physical characterisation difficult. articles.title: Effects of a Nuclear Detonation in Low Earth Orbit
articles.summary: More than 13,000 satellites operate in low Earth orbit (LEO), and concern has grown that nuclear weapons could be used in space to target them. articles.summary: Context. Hercules X-1 (Her X-1) is a well-studied X-ray binary exhibiting superorbital modulation of its X-ray flux. articles.title: Forecasting Fundamental-Plane Tests of Intermediate-mass Black Holes in Radio-selected Dwarf Galaxies

articles.title: Advances in High-Precision Astrometry for Exoplanet Detection for Astrometric Missions
articles.summary: High-precision astrometry is a cornerstone for detecting Earth-like exoplanets in the habitable zones of nearby solar-type stars and probing the nature of dark matter in galactic environments. articles.summary: We present new developments in the mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of the causal and stable first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamic theory by Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha, and Kovtun (BDNK) in general spacetimes. articles.title: Constraints on Cosmic-Rays and the MeV Emission from Jupiter's Atmosphere
articles.summary: The Cosmic $γ$-ray Background (CGB) in the MeV regime remains among the least understood components of diffuse cosmic radiation, primarily due to instrumental limitations in detecting faint isotropic emission at MeV energies. articles.title: Validation of Habitable Zone Limits with a New Radiative-Convective Equilibrium Climate Model
